Title: Ukraine's former defense minister calls for elections and denounces corruption, defying Zelensky
Description: Mykhailo Fedorov, whose dismissal triggered a political crisis in Ukraine, called for presidential elections to be held despite the ongoing war, breaking a taboo since the start of Russia's invasion.

The radio station and underground schools offering Afghan women glimmers of hope
Description: 'Voices of Afghan Women' (3/6). Radio Begum, 'a radio station made by women for women,' is the only connection to the outside world for many Afghan women. It is one of several projects to help young girls access education under the Taliban regime.

Title: Morocco's youth are desperate to reach Ceuta: 'No one throws their child into the water for no reason'
Description: Morocco's youth are increasingly educated and connected, yet face precarious living conditions, low wages and a cost of living that makes independence unattainable. Some described a sense of hopelessness, which, at the end of July, drove many of them to attempt to swim to the Spanish enclave of Ceuta.

Title: Do you wake up at the same time every night? It's nothing to worry about, but if you want to fall back asleep, don't check the time
Description: 'Strange Nights' (6/7). Everyone wakes up several times a night, most often at the end of a sleep cycle. Deep sleepers don't remember it, while others struggle to go back to sleep. To understand this, let's look at how sleep cycles work.

Title: 'Fjord' by Cristian Mungiu, Cannes Palme d'Or winner: A clash of opposing worlds
Description: A deeply religious Romanian evangelical family, newly settled in a small Norwegian town, clashes with the country's liberal principles and ultimately the courts when the couple is suspected of child abuse.

Description: If she were to win, far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has pledged to call a referendum to revise the Constitution and enshrine the far right's core principles in it. According to a member of the highest administrative court, this would be 'a double coup d'état, both in form and content.'

Title: Jean Hegland, American novelist: 'The idea that humans must dominate the Earth and animals has not served us well'
Description: In an interview with Le Monde, the author of the cult novel 'Into the Forest' calls for thinking beyond infinite growth, which she sees as incompatible with protecting the living world.

Title: Mahmoud Darwish and Tamar Ben Ami: The impossible love of a Palestinian poet and an Israeli dancer
Description: In the early 1960s, in Haifa, Israel, the young Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish fell in love with Tamar Ben Ami, a Jewish Israeli dancer. Their romance was intense but brief. From this forbidden love, the writer composed a poignant poem, 'Rita and the Rifle,' which is still sung throughout the Arab world.
